cluster_name: Typhoon Dujuan strikes Japan killing nine, forces mass evacuation
event_summary: Typhoon Dujuan struck Japan's Pacific coast on September 22–23, 2026, killing at least nine people and leaving four missing, while triggering landslides and flooding that knocked out power to 45,000 homes and prompted evacuation advisories for over one million people near Tokyo.
tldr: The most isolated item in the corpus is a Xinhua English article dated October 2017 about Typhoon Lan — a different storm entirely — that appears as a probable cluster contaminant, drawn in by semantic overlap with Japan typhoon coverage. Across the remaining outlets, coverage converges unusually tightly on humanitarian impact — deaths, rescues, mass evacuation — with almost no editorial divergence despite spanning eight countries and two languages. Vietnam’s VnExpress was the sole outlet to lead with a cultural-economic angle: the typhoon cut short the Tokyo Game Show, described as “one of the world’s biggest video game fairs.” India’s The Hindu was uniquely explicit in placing Dujuan within a global 2026 extreme-weather pattern: “the latest extreme weather ‌event in a year of ‌unusually heavy rain, floods and ⁠tropical cyclones that have hit regions across the globe.” Death toll estimates range from two (early Malay Mail reports, Tuesday) to nine (Japan Times, Wednesday morning), reflecting rolling updates rather than editorial disagreement.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Unique lead angle: the typhoon 'cuts short one of the world's biggest video game fairs' (Tokyo Game Show) — the only outlet to connect this disaster to a major cultural-commercial event rather than leading with casualties.
Only outlet to explicitly embed Dujuan in a 2026 global extreme-weather pattern, citing impacts 'from East Asia to North America and Europe' — a climate-context frame absent from all other outlets.
Article dated October 2017 about Typhoon Lan — a different storm entirely — appears as a probable cluster contaminant; the only item in the corpus not covering Typhoon Dujuan.
Carries the highest confirmed death toll in the corpus (nine dead, four missing as of Wednesday morning), several hours ahead of the 4–5 figures in outlets reporting Tuesday evening.
Portuguese-language coverage is the only outlet to specify 500mm of rainfall on a single island — a concrete hydrological measure absent from all English-language reports.

Pre-landfall meteorological tracker (published before the storm hit) noted Dujuan had briefly weakened to a tropical storm on Sunday before restrengthening — storm-track context not provided by any other outlet.

bottom_line: Coverage of Typhoon Dujuan’s strike on the Tokyo region was unusually convergent across eight countries: nearly every outlet focused on the same humanitarian metrics — deaths, mass evacuation, power outages, flight cancellations — with minimal editorial differentiation. The notable exceptions are Vietnam’s VnExpress leading with the Tokyo Game Show disruption, India’s The Hindu placing the storm in a global 2026 extreme-weather pattern, and a 2017 Xinhua article about Typhoon Lan that appears as a cluster contaminant.
